summary: Halyard template titled and recited as mutual, but Lumina's edits make the definition and notification duty protect only Lumina, delete two carve-outs, narrow the evidence standard and add a 12-month exclusivity restriction, with a comment requesting French or Swiss law.

findings.quote: of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] or any member of its Group, which is disclosed by or on behalf of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] to [[DEL: the Receiving Party]][[INS: Halyard]] in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: The edited definition covers only information disclosed by Lumina to Halyard, so the agreement recited as mutual protects only the counterparty.
findings.draft_redline: Confidential Information means any information, however conveyed or presented, that relates to the business, affairs, operations, customers, processes, budgets, pricing, product roadmaps, software, source code, technical specifications, algorithms, know-how or trade secrets of the Disclosing Party or any member of its Group, which is disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose ...
findings.note_to_counterparty: This is a mutual NDA and Halyard will also be sharing information about its platform, so the definition needs to protect both parties. We have restored the original Disclosing Party and Receiving Party wording.

findings.quote: [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] to [[DEL: the Receiving Party]][[INS: Halyard]] in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: The definition of Confidential Information now covers only one party's information, which the playbook lists as a deviation.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate the Disclosing Party / Receiving Party references in clause 1.1.2 so that either Party's information is covered.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please accept the reciprocal definition so that information either party discloses for the Purpose is protected.

findings.quote: [[DEL: Each Party]][[INS: Halyard]] shall immediately notify [[DEL: the other Party]][[INS: Lumina]] in writing
findings.why: The notification and assistance duty is now imposed on Halyard alone in favour of Lumina, and the added reciprocal sentence is ineffective because the definition no longer covers Halyard's information.
findings.draft_redline: Each Party shall immediately notify the other Party in writing if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected unauthorised use, copying or disclosure of any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and shall provide all reasonable assistance to the Disclosing Party in connection with any action or proceedings which the Disclosing Party may institute in respect of such unauthorised use, copying or disclosure.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored clause 2.2 so that the notification duty applies equally to both parties, which makes the added reciprocal sentence unnecessary.

findings.quote: not enter into any commercial discussions or integration partnerships with any third party offering software solutions directly competitive with the Disclosing Party's core analytics products in the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom
findings.why: The inserted wording restricts dealing with competitors of the Disclosing Party for the term plus twelve months, which is an exclusivity or non-compete restriction.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: Halyard is not able to accept restrictions on dealing with third parties in a confidentiality agreement. The confidentiality and use restrictions already protect your information.

findings.quote: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, which is now framed as a named integration project.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: 3.1.3 [[DEL: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party
findings.why: The carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party has been deleted, so one of the four required carve-outs is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: The standard carve-outs for third-party receipt and independent development are needed to keep the obligations workable for both parties, so we have reinstated them.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 [[DEL: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent development carve-out has been deleted, so a further required carve-out is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please accept reinstatement of the independent development carve-out, which is standard and applies equally to both parties.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous written and dated documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from written records or other reasonable evidence to contemporaneous dated documentary evidence only.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer to keep the original evidence standard of written records or other reasonable evidence, which is workable for both parties.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (including advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is permitted on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party remaining liable.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to the minimum extent required by an order of any court of competent jurisdiction or any regulatory, judicial, governmental or similar body
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and an automated backup and legal retention exception (clause 6.2) with continuing confidentiality (clause 6.3).

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party (or its licensors, as applicable)
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and clause 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is as is, with no warranty, a fraud carve-out in 7.4 and a no-obligation-to-proceed statement in 7.5.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual restriction on announcements without prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are expected and any other personal data requires a separate DPA first; the added EU GDPR and French law references do not change this.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice, three-year survival and indefinite protection for Trade Secrets in clause 10.3.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief for any threatened or actual breach of this Agreement by the other Party
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief with cumulative remedies under clause 11.2.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: The reverse engineering prohibition is retained unchanged.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Mutual no-assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales
findings.why: Governing law is England and Wales with exclusive jurisdiction of its courts in clause 12.11; the clause text itself is unchanged.

findings.quote: our group policy is to request French law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of Lyon (Tribunal de commerce de Lyon), or failing that, neutral governing law and jurisdiction in Switzerland
findings.why: The margin comment asks for French law and exclusive Lyon jurisdiction, or Swiss law and courts, which is a request to move away from England and Wales.
findings.draft_redline: This Agreement ... shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales, and each Party submits to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Halyard is not able to agree to French or Swiss law, but we can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts, which would let either party bring proceedings in Lyon where appropriate.
